statement: A planar Laman graph on at least two vertices admits a positive-edge-length assignment with a nontrivial continuous real flex if and only if it is not a 2-tree.

answer.display: Flexible positive-length specializations exist exactly for non-2-trees

scope: Real quasi-injective realizations modulo planar rigid motions: adjacent vertices must be distinct, but nonadjacent vertices may coincide.
notes: The new theorem characterizes which graphs have such exceptional fibers, not the full discriminant or the number of its components. A 2-tree is built from one edge by successively adding a vertex adjacent to both endpoints of an existing edge.
